title: Bassoon
summary: Limits first: one page is posted, D2, and it is a note but not yet the recorded one: 41 cents sharp of the recording (76.4 Hz against the recording's 74.6 Hz), 2.1 semitones too bright in its spectral centroid. Since its second render of 2026-11-23 it carries the clarinet pages' reed-slit turbulence noise (Oldham and Ukpoho's duct-constriction law, an extrapolation, its duct taken as the reed channel), which brought its harmonics-to-noise ratio from 73.8 dB (no noise at all) to 41.1 dB against the recording's 38.7 dB: 7 of 15 measures inside the loose ruler, 4 inside the strict, D 22.52 (before the noise: 5, 4, D 27.63). It sounds only at the flow-fit closing pressure (7.1 kPa) with player Bn1's ff blowing pressure (2648 Pa), while the recording is mf; at the structural 9.5 kPa, and at mf, the model is silent. Two changes of 2026-11-23 made the note. (1) The reed's stiffness and mass are now in the coordinate of the opening h, 247 N/m and 3.64e-6 kg, half the per-blade products the cards carried before, because Grothe's x is one blade's displacement (h = h_inf - 2x, Eqs. 3.12 and 3.18; found by IcyPrairie); the reed frequency, 1311 Hz, is unchanged. (2) One row on the rendered card adds the reed's own channel ahead of the bocal: Grothe's internal volume of 1.9 cm3, which Grothe gives as a reasonable value, an assumption, shaped as one DECLARED cylinder 45 mm long of radius 3.67 mm. That row is on the card only, because the description grammar has no reed-channel row for a double reed yet; a measured channel is being hunted. Neither change alone gave a note: with the correction alone three corners of the grid stay silent and the fourth sounds without a period; with the volume alone the other three corners stay silent. The assembly: the Heckel1-O-Murry body (Johann Adam Heckel, 18 keys, c. 1840-50, Murry Collection; Hichwa-Rachor database sheets, list v48 of 7 March 2025; numbers only, no sheet committed) with 23 tone holes on a 2382.7 mm unfolded column; the bocal of a Grenser bassoon (Historisches Museum Basel 1904.312), another maker and date, whose two printed end diameters (4.2 and 9.8 mm) carry a straight cone declared here; and the reed numbers of one plastic Selmer 270M reed in an artificial mouth (Grothe 2014, Table 3.2). It is a stand-in: not the instrument of the Iowa recordings, whose system is not known, and not a modern bassoon. Before the correction (2026-11-12), a 2 x 2 grid of printed values followed (closing pressure 9.5 kPa, the structural curve, or 7.1 kPa, the flow fit of the same table; blowing pressure 1961 Pa mf, the mean of the up and down rows of Bn1, or 2648 Pa ff, the up row of Bn1 alone; Fuks and Sundberg 1996). 9.5 kPa with 1961 Pa, 7.1 kPa with 1961 Pa (ratio 0.276) and 9.5 kPa with 2648 Pa (ratio 0.279) are silent: exactly zero from 0.6 s to 2.3 s, attack rms 1.63e-3, 1.61e-3 and 1.94e-3 Pa. 7.1 kPa with 2648 Pa (ratio 0.373) sounds, 1.89 Pa rms from 0.6 s to 2.3 s, steady, peak 8.60 Pa, nothing clipped, but it is not periodic: the autocorrelation peak is 0.746 where the criterion fixed before the run asked 0.9 for a note. Its spectral lines are 158.25 Hz and its multiples and 74.98 Hz + k x 158.25 Hz (k = 0 to 3); the 74.98 Hz line is 36 cents above D2 (73.42 Hz) and 22.6 dB under the strongest line (549.7 Hz). All four clips are one binary (music_render build b6g, md5 3177812b24a7) and one card but for the named values.
physics_present: the Heckel1-O-Murry air column as a numbers-only table, each row citing its Hichwa-Rachor sheet row: 23 rod-station diameters, 23 tone holes with diameter, depth and distance (the keyed holes from the General Information sheet), the two bores and the U-turn of the boot, the long joint and bell lengths and the receiver choke; the pitch of 440 Hz is the database authors' program input; the wing and boot heights sum to 849.9 mm against the printed 832 mm, 17.9 mm unreconciled (about 13 cents)

the bocal of another instrument (Grenser H3, sheet rows 2 to 6): 4.2 mm at the reed end, 9.8 mm at the wing end (equal to the Heckel1 receiver bore), string 33.3 mm, metal 334 and 314 mm; a straight cone between the two end diameters is DECLARED (the sheet prints no profile): 4.2 mm to 9.224 mm over 290.7 mm, then a 0.576 mm step to the 9.8 mm receiver

the reed numbers of Grothe's Table 3.2, structural column, mapped to the lumped single-reed owner: rest opening 1 mm, width 9.3 mm, closing pressure 9.5 kPa (flow fit 7.1 kPa), stiffness 247 N/m and mass 3.64e-6 kg in the coordinate of the opening h (half the per-blade products K S_r and mu_r S_r, because Grothe's x is one blade's displacement, h = h_inf - 2x; until 2026-11-23 the cards carried the per-blade 494 N/m and 7.28e-6 kg), damping ratio 0.1163; the face area the engine implies (stiffness over closing pressure times rest opening) is now the printed S_r of 26 mm2 at 9.5 kPa (34.8 mm2 at the 7.1 kPa of the posted page), and Grothe gives S_r and Q_r only to a factor 2

the reed's own channel, on the posted D2 card only (not yet a description row): Grothe's internal volume of 1.9 cm3, given as a reasonable value, an assumption (Grothe's other value, 2.2 cm3, is a fitted guess and is not used), as one DECLARED cylinder 45 mm long of radius 3.67 mm between the blade tip and the bocal; 1.0 cm3 gave no period

turbulence noise at the reed slit (the posted D2 page since 2026-11-23T06:28Z; rows reed.constriction_noise_seed and reed.constriction_noise_duct_radius_m of description-d2-c71ff): the clarinet pages' `constriction_noise` row, Oldham and Ukpoho's printed K(St) duct-constriction law (J. Sound Vib. 1990) as a seeded third-octave pressure source at the slit, rms K times the held blowing pressure, silent while the flow is not forward; an EXTRAPOLATION in size, speed and shape, its duct the reed channel's declared 3.67 mm radius (the bocal's printed 2.1 mm reed end, rendered beside it before either was graded, gave 5 of 15 loose, 4 strict, D 23.53)

Fuks and Sundberg 1996 blowing pressures of player Bn1 at D2, kept as player data: mf 1961 Pa (mean of up 21 and down 19 cm H2O) and ff 2648 Pa (up row, 27 cm H2O; the mean of the two ff rows would be 2550 Pa)

the D2 fingering, tone holes 20, 22 and 23 counted from the reed end open and all others closed, read from Almenraeder 1824 Tabelle II, a 15-key chart of another instrument used as a DECLARED stand-in: the plate prints no legend (filled = closed is inferred from its first column), the D2 column's second row is a smudged outline read as open, the row-to-hole identity is probable, and holes with no plate row take the closed rest state by declaration

generic fs-duct conical and cylindrical segments, tone-hole side branches, a flanged bell load, the lumped single-reed owner and the physical baffled outlet receiver already run for the clarinet, now given this geometry in four renders (the exhaled-breath gas pack, 20 C dry room air, 2.65 s)

numerical settings, not measurements: a 48 kHz mechanics clock (the oboe's 96 kHz made the characteristic-line ladder of this 2.38 m bore refuse), a line_ladder row of 1e-10 and 131072 taps; a passive-sweep check planned for this card was dropped, the n3d build (md5 650c26c00a2c) printing no impedance lines for these cards, so no sweep could be read (its unplanned renders of s1, s2 and d2 were silent, rms 9.6e-4, 8.8e-4 and 6.8e-4 Pa)
physics_missing: a note: C3 and every pitch but D2 are not built; C3's plate column needs the chart's right-hand table, whose rows r10 and r11 are keys of unidentified holes; no fingering chart is printed for the Heckel1; the all-holes-closed and bell-hole-open states were not rendered

a note at the recording's dynamic: the posted D2 sounds only at the flow-fit closing pressure with Bn1's ff pressure (the recording is mf) and is 41 cents sharp; at 9.5 kPa, and at mf, every reed volume tried (1.0, 1.9 and 2.2 cm3) is silent; the reed numbers are one plastic reed's in an artificial mouth on modern bocals, not a cane reed of the 1840s

a measured reed channel (its volume and shape) and the pressure recovery from the reed's opening into the staple: the posted volume is assumed and its cylinder declared; a noise source measured on a double reed (the posted noise is a duct-constriction law extrapolated to the slit, and the cepstral envelope gap grew with it, 8.8 to 10.2 dB)
a player: one fixed blowing pressure of one modern player (Bn1), no lip or embouchure row, no tongue, no vocal tract; no blowing pressure measured on a bassoon of the 1840s
pad lift and key rise (the sheets give none), tone-hole undercut and edge rounding (the sheet notes undercutting), chimney heights (the sheet's depth readings stand in)
the bocal's measured profile (only its two end diameters are printed) and the 17.9 mm of the wing and boot heights
the reference of the keyed holes' distances (near edge or centre; not stated), and the low Eb and low C# 'from the small tenon', read from the bottom tenon, an assumption
the instrument of the Iowa recordings, the comparison target: its system, maker and pitch are not known
blocked: C3 and every further pitch: the Almenraeder plate's right-hand table has keys of unidentified holes (rows r10 and r11) and no fingering chart is printed for the Heckel1; needs the instrument's own chart or an identification of those keys. D2 at the recording's mf: not reached; the posted note needs Bn1's ff pressure and the flow-fit closing pressure, and its reed volume is an assumption (a hunt for a measured bassoon reed channel and its pressure recovery is open). A modern German-system bore: a hunt of 2026-11-12 found one printed source of measured bores, James L. Burton's Eastman School of Music dissertation 'Bassoon bore dimensions' (1975; University of Rochester repository, hdl 1802/38249), which tabulates the bore diameters of 65 German-system bassoons, Heckels among them, at one-inch intervals (Appendix C, pages 119 to 249; the bocal and the tone holes are not measured). Its copyright page says that no part of the work, 'including the use of measurement data for further research', may be used without permission, so none of its numbers is used here; asking for that permission is the owner's decision. T. Grothe's dissertation on bassoon acoustics (TU Dresden), the source of the reed row, prints no bore or tone-hole table of the bassoons it measured.
